summary: Lewis County, WA lookout site where a cabin stood from 1940 until abandonment in 1965; Elmer Balch was the lookout in 1956; a 2020 wind turbine erased the remnants.

facts.design: Cabin built 1940; replaced in 1954 by a cabin the register calls a U.S. Army cabin
facts.status_note: Abandoned 1965 and no longer standing; a 2020 wind turbine obliterated the last remnants

staffing.status: staffed; Elmer Balch on fire watch

access.note: Willhite: site is part of the Weyerhaeuser Vail Tree Farm, where permits are likely required; the wind farm probably adds restrictions

events.note: Newspaper item (Chehalis Bee-Nugget, as quoted by Forest Lookouts) on a phone line installed at Hunter's cabin; Willhite thinks the elevation matches the lookout site
Cabin constructed on the site in 1940 (register, firelookout.com; Kresek inventory via Willhite). Willhite says the origin date of the site is unknown
Lookout cabin visible in aerial photos
New cabin at the site; register and firelookout.com call it a U.S. Army cabin
Elmer Balch on fire watch at Hunter's Cabin that summer (Daily Chronicle, June 1956); Willhite names him as lookout
Last remaining remnants obliterated by construction of a wind turbine for the Skookumchuck Wind Farm
Registered April 3, 2020; nominated by Tammy McLeod

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and firelookout.com give 2,681 ft (817 m); Willhite gives 2,695 ft but says early maps show 2,681. The story gives both figures.

Register and firelookout.com date the first cabin to 1940, and the Kresek inventory agrees; Willhite says the site's origin date is unknown and a trail to Hunters Cabin existed by 1916. 1940 is the earliest documented cabin on the site.

notes_for_editor: Brief access 'unknown' replaced by permission, from Willhite's note on Weyerhaeuser permits. The brief flagged 'They share a register number' without naming the other record; the register gives US 1970 for this site and I did not identify the other holder. Willhite says the Firefinder map centers on the cabin/benchmark site about a mile away and that this was an error; the 1941 USGS benchmark 'HUNTERS CABIN 1941' is not the lookout. The 1925 phone line may refer to the lookout or the cabin; the story says so.
